chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House seven times as the obligatory circumambulation, then performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then he had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: He should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate three circuits, and seek forgiveness of his Lord, and there is nothing upon him.

I said: But if he had performed the obligatory circumambulation of the House, then circumambulated four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then had intercourse with his wife? He said: His Hajj is spoiled, and upon him is a camel (as expiation), and he should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate seven circuits, then perform Sa'ee, and seek forgiveness of his Lord.

I said: Why did you not make it upon him, when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his Sa'ee, just as you made upon him a sacrificial offering when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his circumambulation? He said: Indeed, the circumambulation is obligatory, and therein is prayer, and the Sa'ee is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

I said: Is it not that Allah says, 'Surely As-Safa and Al-Marwa are among the rituals of Allah'? He said: Yes, but He has said regarding them, 'And whoever does good voluntarily, then surely Allah is Grateful, Knowing'. So, if the Sa'ee were obligatory, He would not have said, 'And whoever does good voluntarily'.

key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Sa'ee (ritual walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.غَمَزَهُ بَطْنُهُ: His belly ached (urgency to relieve himself)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in Hajj rulings if a man has intercourse with his wife before or after completing the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic distinction between obligatory (fard) and sunnah acts within Hajj, specifically contrasting the status of Tawaf al-Ifadah with Sa'ee. Imam al-Sadiq (as) argues that since Sa'ee is classified as a Sunnah based on the Quranic phrase 'whoever volunteers good,' its interruption does not invalidate the core ritual like the obligatory Tawaf does. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on textual interpretation of Quranic grammar to determine ritual hierarchy and expiation requirements.
